entities.summary:
Operation Rheinübung was a 1941 German battle that took place in the Atlantic Ocean, involving the battleship Bismarck and the heavy cruiser Prinz Eugen. Between May 18 and May 27, the German ships clashed with the British Royal Navy, resulting in the sinking of the Bismarck on May 27. This battle was a significant turning point in the Battle of the Atlantic, as it highlighted the German U-boat threat and led to increased Allied convoy escorts.

The battle was a tactical victory for the British, but it came at a great cost. The Bismarck, with its 30.5 cm main guns, was one of the most powerful battleships in the world, and its loss was a significant blow to the German navy. The battle also marked the beginning of the end of the German U-boat campaign, as the Allies increased their convoy escorts and implemented new tactics to counter the submarines.

The legacy of Operation Rheinübung can be seen in the increased Allied convoy escorts and the development of new tactics to counter the German U-boats. The battle also marked a turning point in the Battle of the Atlantic, as the Allies began to gain the upper hand. In the end, the German U-boat campaign was unable to stem the flow of supplies to Britain, and the Allies were able to maintain their grip on the seas.

The Bismarck's sinking was a significant moment in the history of the Battle of the Atlantic, and it marked the beginning of the end of the German U-boat campaign. As one historian noted, 'The sinking of the Bismarck was a major blow to the German navy, and it marked the beginning of the end of the German U-boat campaign.'
